purpose: R-audit: does the 3-layer perovskite stress device reproduce its archived converged outcome on the review-fix tree?
archived_record: docs/paper/records/solver_fallback.json claims: converged=true, max_residual=2.19e-8, efficiency=1.7%, fallback_used=[true,true,true,true,true], V=[0,.25,.5,.75,1.0]

current_result.note: sweep DIVERGES above V~0.25V (fallback stops firing at biases 3-4)

verdict: REGRESSION / non-reproducibility: the shipped code does NOT reproduce the archived 'converges to 1e-8' claim for the 3-layer perovskite on the exact same inputs. The current run diverges at high bias and falls back to best-iterate with garbage PCE. Either the archived record was from a different code revision, or a continuity/globalization change between 0.1.16+ and the review tree broke convergence on this stiff device.
impact: solver_fallback.json's headline 'sweep converges to ~1e-8' is not reproducible on the review-fix tree; the record must be flagged OR-REPRODUCE or the convergence regression fixed.

root_cause.finding: Reproduced the archived record ONLY when called exactly as the script does (default ls=None -> raw 899.9 W/m2).

normalized_spectrum_ls.cause: Passing spectrum(normalize=True) (1000 W/m2) changes the generation scale ~11%; on the rank-deficient Jacobian (dense kappa ~4e45) the extra drive pushes biases 3-4 past the lstsq-fallback recovery radius, so dgbsv raises and the sweep diverges instead of converging at ~1e-8.

root_cause.meta: Even in the converging case, Voc=nan and Jsc~0 (efficiency 1.7% is a numerical trace, not a physical operating point). The device remains NOT a working solar cell; it is a singular-matrix stress test whose numerical outcome is fragile to incident-power scaling.

positive_control_working_pin.question: Does a properly-structured perovskite p-i-n converge and give a sensible J-V (ruling out 'the solver cant handle perovskite')?

device.material: pvk Eg=1.55 Chi=3.9 eps=24 Nc=2.2e18 Nv=1.8e19 mn=20 mp=20 A=2e5 tn=1e-6 tp=1e-6

result.iv_shape: monotonic decreasing; forward current +11.9 mA/cm^2 at V=0 crosses zero at Voc=0.964V, sweeps to -17 mA/cm^2 at V=1.0V  (correct diode quadrant)

positive_control_working_pin.interpretation: The p-i-n converges to machine precision and shows the textbook diode J-V. Jsc (12 mA/cm^2) is lower than the ~35 mA/cm^2 textbook perovskite because the model uses a thin (dimensionless) absorber and Beer-Lambert optics; the package's own Si reference targets ~17 mA/cm^2 by the same calibration, so this is the model's normal regime — not a defect. The solver handles perovskite parameters correctly.
positive_control_working_pin.verdict: The 3-layer n-p-n failure is STRUCTURAL (no hole path), not a material/handling limitation. A correct p-i-n works.
